description: Twenty is a platform that generates per‑workspace REST and GraphQL APIs from your schema, letting you create, read, update, and delete built‑in and custom records while programmatically managing objects, fields, and relationships.

mcp.details: Twenty's server implements MCP‑compliant OAuth discovery endpoints, providing path‑aware protected‑resource metadata and advertising required MCP parameters.

evidence.claim: Twenty implements OAuth 2.0 with authorization code + PKCE for user-facing apps and client credentials for server-to-server access.
Internal scripts, automation use API Key authentication.
External app acting on behalf of a user uses OAuth — Authorization Code.
Server-to-server, no user context uses OAuth — Client Credentials.
Twenty's authentication system supports API keys, OAuth tokens, and JWT.
Include the API key in the Authorization header as a Bearer token.
Send a Bearer token with each request via the Authorization header.
Twenty provides REST and GraphQL APIs generated from the workspace schema.
Core API is available via /rest/ and /graphql/ endpoints.
Metadata API is also available as REST and GraphQL.
Base URL for cloud is https://api.twenty.com/.
Authentication uses Bearer API keys.
OAuth-based access is supported for external apps.
Twenty provides a REST API for CRUD operations on CRM data.
Free trial signup provides API access
API key created in Settings → API & Webhooks
API included in free trial, no paid plan required
Twenty's server aligns its OAuth discovery metadata with the MCP authorization specification (draft).
The server splits protected‑resource metadata by path (/.well-known/oauth-protected-resource and /.well-known/oauth-protected-resource/mcp) to meet MCP and RFC 9728 requirements.
It advertises the authorization_response_iss_parameter_supported flag as true to satisfy MCP and OAuth 2.1 security BCP.
